title: Module 5 - Corporate Issuers and Equity Valuation

assets.alt_text: Corporate valuation map from capital allocation and operating forecasts through FCFF or FCFE and matched discount rates to enterprise value, equity value, thesis, and monitoring.
assets.prompt: Create a 1920x1080 PNG, 16:9. Academic corporate value-creation and equity-valuation map for Module 5. Show governance and capital allocation feeding operating forecasts and ROIC, then two matched valuation paths: FCFF with WACC to enterprise value, and FCFE with cost of equity to equity value. Include the bridge from enterprise value to common equity value, followed by thesis, risks, catalysts, and monitoring. Use short labels only. Off-white background, navy linework, teal cash-flow paths, amber discount-rate highlights, coral risk markers, and a 7% safe margin. No fake company, price target, or numerical valuation.
production_notes: Original deterministic figure authored in this repository for the book; no external image or third-party data are incorporated.
Generated from code to preserve the FCFF-WACC and FCFE-cost-of-equity matching rules.
The diagram communicates method selection and governance, not an investment recommendation.

assets.alt_text: Two-panel figure for the simulated expansion project. The left panel shows the USD 110m time-zero outlay, USD 28m operating cash flows in Years 1 through 5, and separate USD 18m Year 5 recovery and salvage. The right panel shows NPV declining with the effective annual required return, crossing zero at the 12.39% IRR; NPV at 10% is USD 7.32m.
assets.prompt: Render an exact 1600x900 PNG with the annual project cash-flow timeline beside its NPV profile. Separate Year 5 operating cash flow from terminal working-capital recovery and salvage, identify discrete and interpolated payback conventions, and mark both NPV at 10% and the IRR zero crossing.
production_notes: Original deterministic figure authored in this repository for the book; no external image or third-party data are incorporated.
The timeline and NPV profile use the lesson's single cash-flow vector and annual end-of-year convention.
Hatching, markers, and line styles supplement color for accessibility.

assets.alt_text: Line chart of simulated effective annual USD required returns at 20%, 33%, 45%, and 55% target debt to capital. WACC is 8.28%, 8.33%, 8.81%, and 9.93% as relevered cost of equity and after-tax debt cost change with leverage.
assets.prompt: Render an exact 1600x900 PNG with the four simulated target-capital-structure scenarios and recalculated cost of equity, after-tax cost of debt, and WACC. Use exact percentage labels, a zero baseline, line styles and markers in addition to color, and the canonical book palette.
production_notes: Original deterministic figure authored in this repository for the book; no external image or third-party data are incorporated.
The chart is generated from the same Hamada-style beta and WACC equations used in the lesson.
All values are labeled as simulated effective annual USD teaching assumptions on a nominal, inflation-inclusive basis.

assets.alt_text: Two-panel waterfall for the simulated subscription forecast. Revenue of USD 26.640m reconciles through gross profit and operating expense to EBIT of USD 6.648m; NOPAT of USD 4.986m then reconciles through depreciation, capital expenditure, and working capital to FCFF of USD 3.886m.
assets.prompt: Render an exact 1600x900 PNG with a two-stage waterfall from simulated revenue to NOPAT and from NOPAT to FCFF. Keep depreciation's expense and add-back roles visually distinct, label every amount, and reconcile exactly to the lesson's forecast table.
production_notes: Original deterministic figure authored in this repository for the book; no external image or third-party data are incorporated.
All bars are generated from one tested forecast anatomy rather than hand-entered chart labels.
The chart uses hatching as well as color and explicitly labels the annual USD simulation.

assets.alt_text: Annotated three-by-three DCF sensitivity matrix for simulated value per diluted share. Values rise as WACC falls or perpetual growth rises; the outlined base case at 9% WACC and 3% growth is USD 11.40 per share.
assets.prompt: Render an exact 1600x900 PNG with the 3x3 DCF value-per-share sensitivity for WACC of 8%, 9%, and 10% and nominal perpetual growth of 2%, 3%, and 4%. Annotate each USD per diluted share result, outline the 9%/3% base cell, and use a zero-centered interpretation around the base case without implying probabilities.
production_notes: Original deterministic figure authored in this repository for the book; no external image or third-party data are incorporated.
The matrix is computed from the lesson's explicit FCFF, terminal value, enterprise-to-equity bridge, and diluted share count.
The diverging color scale shows direction from the worked base case; it is not a probability distribution.
